title: Seoul's Incheon Named Busiest International Airport
paragraphs: South Korea's Incheon International Airport says it has become the world's busiest airport for international passengers for the first time.

The airport, located about 50 kilometers west of Seoul, welcomed 38.4 million international passengers during the first six months of 2026. That was the highest total among over 1,200 airports around the world, according to preliminary data from Airports Council International (ACI).
London's Heathrow Airport came second with 37.8 million international passengers, followed by Singapore's Changi Airport with 34.5 million.
Incheon opened in 2001, and has moved up the list over the years. It was 10th in the world in 2002, fifth in 2018, and third in both 2024 and 2025.

One reason for its rise this year is the US-Iran conflict, which has affected air travel through the Middle East. Dubai International Airport, which topped the list last year, has seen passenger numbers fall since the conflict began. Some travelers who would usually transfer at airports in the Middle East are now flying through Asia instead, including through Incheon.

More people are also traveling to South Korea, especially from China and Japan, thanks in part to the growing popularity of Korean culture around the world. In the first half of 2026, 39% of Incheon's passengers were foreign travelers, up from 35% for the whole of 2025.

Incheon has also become bigger. An expansion completed in 2024 increased the airport's capacity to 106 million passengers a year. It now serves 101 airlines and offers flights to 158 international destinations.

However, Incheon is only number one for international passengers. America's Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport remains the world's busiest when both domestic and international passengers are included.
